bib.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 34th International Conference on Machine Learning, Sydney, Australia, PMLR 70, 2017

question: Are modern neural network classifiers well calibrated, what causes miscalibration, and which post-processing method fixes it best?
hypothesis: Increased capacity and reduced regularisation (depth, width, Batch Normalization, less weight decay) worsen calibration, and a simple low-dimensional post-hoc correction suffices.
contributions: Show modern deep nets are poorly calibrated, unlike older ones
Identify depth, width, weight decay and Batch Normalization as factors influencing calibration
Compare post-processing calibration methods and introduce temperature scaling (single-parameter Platt scaling), plus vector and matrix scaling extensions

method.summary: Train standard CNN, DAN and TreeLSTM classifiers on 6 image and 4 text datasets, measure ECE/MCE/NLL/error on test sets, then fit post-hoc calibrators (histogram binning, isotonic regression, BBQ, temperature, vector, matrix scaling) on a held-out validation set with the network frozen.
method.task: multiclass classification calibration (image and document classification)

datasets.name: SST Binary / Fine Grained
datasets.source: Socher et al. 2013; split per Tai et al. 2015

models.name: ResNet (110 layers; 50 for Birds/Cars; 152 for ImageNet/SVHN)
ResNet with stochastic depth (SD)
models.architecture: ResNet-110 SD; ResNet-152 SD on SVHN

models.name: DAN 3
models.architecture: Deep Averaging Network, 3 feed-forward layers with Batch Normalization

training.objective: Networks trained with the original papers' recipes (NLL / cross entropy). Calibrators: NLL on validation set for Platt/temperature/vector/matrix scaling; squared loss for binning and isotonic.
training.lr_schedule: Fig 3 run: learning rate drops by 10x at epochs 250 and 375
training.epochs: Fig 3 plots up to about 500 epochs; otherwise per original papers
training.weight_decay: varied 1e-5 to 1e-2 in Fig 2 far right (read from figure)
training.regularisation: Data augmentation and Batch Normalization the only other regularisers in the weight-decay experiment

other.recipe: We use the data preprocessing, training procedures, and hyperparameters as described in each paper. For text: default hyperparmaeters suggested by the authors.
other.calibrator_fit: Each calibration method requires a hold-out validation set, which in practice can be the same set used for hyperparameter tuning.
other.temperature_solver: conjugate gradient solver, optimal T in 10 iterations
other.fig2_setups: depth sweep: ResNet CIFAR-100, 64 filters per layer; width sweep: ResNet-14 CIFAR-100; BN: 6-layer ConvNet CIFAR-100; weight decay: ResNet-110 CIFAR-100 (read from Fig 2 and text)

inference.temperature: T fit on validation set (post-hoc); T=1 during training
inference.samples: Single run per dataset/model/method; no seeds or repeats stated

metrics.name: ECE
metrics.definition: sum over M bins of |B_m|/n * |acc(B_m) - conf(B_m)|, M=15 equal-width bins, top-label confidence

metrics.name: NLL
metrics.unit: % as printed in Table S3 (values like 0.9786)

eval.protocol: Test-set metrics before and after calibrators fit on validation split; single run; no significance testing stated.

evidence.quote: We set T =1 during training, and subsequently ﬁnd its optimal value on the validation set.

results.claim: Typical uncalibrated ECE is 4 to 10%; SVHN and Reuters are below 1%.

results.claim: Temperature scaling outperforms all other methods on the vision tasks and performs comparably on NLP datasets.
results.note: Table 1 has exceptions: on CIFAR-10 ResNet 110 histogram binning and BBQ beat temperature scaling; Cars ResNet 50 histogram binning (1.74%) and BBQ (1.84%) beat it (2.35%)
results.quote: Temperature scaling outperforms all other methods on the vision tasks, and performs comparably to other methods on the NLP datasets.

results.claim: Temperature scaling beats vector and matrix scaling although they are strictly more general; vector scaling learns nearly constant entries.

limits: Cannot claim causality for depth, width, weight decay and BN effects
Why these trends affect calibration while improving accuracy is left to future work
All calibrators need a held-out validation set drawn from the same distribution as test; no distribution shift studied
Reuters not improved by temperature scaling; authors suggest dataset split or binning scheme may affect measurements
MCE is very sensitive to binning scheme and unsuitable for small test sets (Table S1 caption)
Single run per setting, no seeds or confidence intervals; optimiser, learning rate, batch size not restated (deferred to cited papers)
Only top-label calibration, equal-width 15-bin ECE; ImageNet-era 2015-2016 architectures, later work (e.g. transformers) not covered
Training hyperparameters, compute and hardware not reported
